# F12: Urdu narration option

Status: Built 2026-10-01 (signed off the same day under the instruction "continue with the whole development"); the Urdu narration awaits teacher review · Owner: Muhammad Noor Khan · Last updated: 2026-10-01

Plan: [implementation plan, F12](../implementation-plan-subjects-languages-admin-parent.md#f12-urdu-narration-track) · Decisions: D5 (English mix by default, Urdu option), plan decision 6 (the subject teacher reviews the Urdu)

## Problem

Lessons are narrated in Roman Urdu mixed with English, read by an Indian-English voice. Students who think in Urdu find the accent and the English terms hard to follow. They need the same lesson narrated in proper Urdu by a Pakistani voice, without losing the textbook page alongside.

## Users and access rules

| Role | What they can do | What they must never see or do |
|---|---|---|
| Student | Switch the lesson between **English mix** and **اردو**; hearing 90% of either track unlocks the quiz | An Urdu track that a teacher has not approved (outside demo mode) |
| Subject teacher | Approve or request changes to the Urdu narration separately from the lesson | — |
| Parent, college admin | No change | — |

## Screens

- **Lesson player:** a **Narration: English mix | اردو** switch above the caption, shown only when the lesson has an Urdu track.
  - Switching changes the audio, the "Now explaining" caption and the full transcript (Nastaliq, right to left).
  - It keeps the textbook page and the quiz rule.
  - The choice is remembered on the device.
- **Media controls and the progress bar** stay left to right.
- **Desktop:** the switch sits at the top of the side column.

## API and data changes

| Method and path | Who | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/lessons/<id>` | Student | Adds `urdu: {audio, duration, review, script}` when the Urdu track may be shown, else `null` |
| `POST /api/lessons/<id>/progress` | Student | Accepts `track: "mix"` or `"ur"`; heard seconds are kept per track; 90% of either unlocks the quiz |

- **Content Factory:**
  - Authored scripts take an optional `sections_ur` (same page order as `sections`).
  - `build` narrates it with `ur-PK-AsadNeural` (`voice_ur` in the book config) into `audio-ur.mp3`, with its own cue times.
  - `lesson.json` gets `tracks.ur` and a separate `review_ur`.
  - Review it with `python factory.py review phy11 <lesson> --approve --track ur --by "<teacher>"`.
- **Backend:**
  - `Lesson` gains `ur_audio`, `ur_audio_bytes`, `ur_duration_sec`, `ur_sections` and `ur_review_status`.
  - `LessonProgress` gains `heard_secs_ur`.
  - `import_lessons` copies the Urdu audio.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given an authored script with `sections_ur`, when built, then `audio-ur.mp3` is narrated with the Urdu voice, with cue times, and its review starts as draft. Approving it survives an unchanged rebuild and does not approve the main lesson.
2. Given Urdu sections out of page order or on a page outside the lesson, then the build is refused.
3. Given a lesson with an Urdu track, then the lesson response includes it, with Urdu-script sections.
4. Given a student hears 90% of the Urdu track and none of the English mix, then the quiz unlocks.
5. Given an Urdu track still in draft outside demo mode, then it is not offered and its progress is refused. Once approved, it is offered.
6. Given an unknown track name, then the server returns 400.

## Out of scope

- Urdu quiz questions (the quiz stays in the textbook's English).
- Urdu narration for subjects without content.
- A paid voice service. `edge-tts` is free but unofficial; switching to Azure Speech only changes `cf/tts.py:synthesize`.

## Risks and open questions

- **The Urdu script is a first draft written during development.** Technical terms are written phonetically in Urdu script (فورس، ایکسلریشن) so the voice pronounces them reliably. A physics teacher who reads Urdu must check every term and number before it is approved.
- **Pronunciation of formulas** (for example "ایل ٹی کی طاقت منفی دو") needs a listening check by a teacher.

## Definition of done

- [x] Spec signed off, with out-of-scope items listed
- [x] Every acceptance criterion has a passing automated test
- [x] Access-rule tests pass: wrong role, wrong college, wrong class, not linked
- [ ] Screens checked at 360, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px in light and dark mode
- [ ] Accessibility checks pass, with no serious or critical issues
- [ ] Performance budget met on the low-end phone profile
- [ ] Works offline or fails with a clear message (no blank screens)
- [ ] English and Urdu text reviewed by a native speaker
- [ ] Content approved by a subject teacher (if students see it)
- [x] Errors are logged; personal data is not written to the logs
- [x] README or admin guide updated
- [ ] Tried by at least 2 real users; their issues fixed or logged

## Implementation notes

Built on 1 October 2026.

- **Content:** all three Unit 1 lessons now have Urdu narration: 1.1 (13 sections, 3:02), 1.2 (10 sections, 1:51) and 1.3 (12 sections, 3:03), about 0.7–1.1 MB each, voice `ur-PK-AsadNeural`. Each lesson's `review_notes` flags the Urdu as a draft.
- **Progress:** the quiz unlocks on 90% of either track. `heardShare` reports the larger of the two, so the home screen and parent view are unchanged.
- **Font:** the Nastaliq font is loaded when the Urdu track is chosen, even if the rest of the app is in English.

Checks run: 19 Content Factory tests (3 new) and 76 backend tests (3 new). Browser journey at 390 px (English and Urdu interface) and 1280 px: switching to Urdu plays the 1:51 Urdu audio with Urdu captions and transcript, the server records Urdu heard time separately (3.6% Urdu, 0% mix after a few seconds), switching back restores the English mix, and there are no page errors.

## Release report

Filled in one week after release.

All six features in the plan are built and tested: F20, F21, F22 (which includes F5), F3, F23 and F12. All 76 backend tests and 19 Content Factory tests pass, and each feature also passed a browser run at phone and desktop sizes with no page errors. I treated "continue with the whole development" as sign-off for each spec, and recorded that in every spec's status line.

To see it, run `start-demo.bat`. It installs the one new library (`pywebpush`, used for phone notifications), updates your database and reloads the demo data. I checked the new database updates on a copy of your current database. The README demo script has new steps 8–12, one per feature.

| Feature | What it adds |
|---|---|
| **F20 Subjects** | A card per subject; subjects with no lessons and all of Grade 12 show "Coming soon"; teachers request a subject and the college admin approves it |
| **F21 Parent progress** | Attendance, topics done and quiz average per child, topic-by-topic detail, and a weekly summary (`send_weekly_summaries`, scheduled for Sundays) |
| **F22 College admin console** | The college admin (Ms. Sana, 399 4440001) adds and suspends people, creates classes, assigns teachers, imports a roster from a spreadsheet file (checked first, saved all or nothing), approves requests, and has an activity log. Only their own college is visible. The Django panel is now for your team only; `create_college` sets up a new college |
| **F3 Free alerts** | Alerts in the app plus free phone notifications, and a one-tap **Send on WhatsApp** button for each absent student's parent, which uses the teacher's own WhatsApp |
| **F23 Urdu screens** | An **اردو** button switches student and parent screens to right-to-left Urdu; a parent who chooses Urdu gets alerts and the weekly summary in Urdu |
| **F12 Urdu narration** | All three Unit 1 lessons can be heard in Urdu, read by a Pakistani voice, with an Urdu transcript; hearing 90% of either version unlocks the quiz |

I also fixed a rule break in the existing code: the server log printed phone numbers and sign-in codes. It no longer does, and a test checks for it.

**Needs people before real students or parents see it:**
- **Urdu text:** a native speaker should review every sentence in `demo/i18n.js` and the alert texts in `backend/lms/notify.py`. I wrote them, so treat them as drafts.
- **Urdu narration:** a physics teacher who reads Urdu should listen to it and approve it with `factory.py review … --track ur`. The three lessons themselves are also still drafts.
- **Phone notifications:** not yet confirmed on a real phone. My headless browser has no notification service, so only the server side is tested. Try it on this computer at `http://localhost:8000`. Phones need the app on an HTTPS address, so they'll work once it's hosted.

**Other things to know:**

# Stitch prompts for the EduSaas UI

As of 1 October 2026 · For: Google Stitch (AI UI design) · Feeds: F1, the React rebuild

This pack describes every screen of the EduSaas app so Stitch can design them in one consistent style. The designs then guide F1. The design tokens below are the ones the app uses today, so the designs and the code stay in step.

## How to use it

1. Create one Stitch project called **EduSaas**. Choose **Mobile** first.
2. Paste the **master prompt** (section 1) as the first message. It sets the product, users, brand and components for every later screen.
3. Paste the screen prompts (section 2) one at a time, in the same project, so Stitch reuses the style. Each prompt stands on its own if you need to regenerate one.
4. After the mobile screens, run the **variant prompts** (section 3) for desktop, dark mode and Urdu.
5. Check every screen against the **review checklist** (section 4) before exporting to Figma or code.

Notes:
- **Textbook pages:** Stitch can't show the real National Book Foundation pages. Prompts ask for a "scanned textbook page placeholder", and the real page goes in during build.
- **People:** every name and phone number is fictional (the demo uses the unissued `+92 399` range).
- **Iterating:** keep prompts short when you revise one screen, for example "Make the Submit button sticky above the bottom bar."

---

## 1. Master prompt (paste first)

```text
Design a mobile-first web app (installable PWA) called EduSaas, for FBISE intermediate colleges in Pakistan.

WHAT IT DOES: When a student misses a class, they get the exact textbook lesson they missed as a narrated page: the scanned textbook page on screen, with audio narration that follows the page. After listening to 90% they take a 5-question quiz; 4 correct = "Cleared for class". The parent gets an alert, and the teacher sees a green "Cleared" tick. The college admin registers everyone. The only way in is a phone number registered by the college.

USERS (4 roles, each with their own home screen):
- Student (16–18, low-end Android phone, patchy mobile data): catches up on missed lessons, studies by subject.
- Teacher: takes attendance in under a minute, sees who is cleared, tells parents on WhatsApp with one tap.
- Parent (often reads Urdu more easily than English, may not be tech-savvy): sees their child's attendance, progress and alerts. Read-only.
- College admin: adds teachers, students and parents, imports a class from a spreadsheet, approves teachers' subject requests.

BRAND AND STYLE: calm, trustworthy, academic. Flat surfaces, 1px borders, soft 12px corners, no heavy shadows, no gradients, no stock photos, no emoji. Generous spacing. Feels like a well-made banking or government-services app, not a game.

COLOURS (light theme):
- Background #F5F6F9, cards #FFFFFF, sunken areas #EEF0F5, borders #DDE1EA
- Text #1B2130, secondary text #5A6478
- Primary (deep navy) #1E3A5F, text on primary #FFFFFF
- Accent (teal/emerald) #0F8F83, accent tint #E3F4F2
- Success #047857 on #E3F5EC; Pending/warning (amber) #A55A06 on #FFF3DC; Error/absent #B42318 on #FDECEA
- WhatsApp green for WhatsApp actions only: #128C7E
COLOURS (dark theme): background #171A21, cards #21252E, borders #353B47, text #ECEEF3, secondary #A3ABBB, primary #7AA7E8, accent #3CC9B8, success #4ADE9B, warning #F5B94A, error #F58A80.

TYPE: Inter (or Roboto). Body 16px minimum, line height 1.5. H1 22px bold on phones (26px desktop). Section labels 15px bold, uppercase, letter-spaced, secondary colour. Urdu text uses Noto Nastaliq Urdu with line height 2 and right-to-left layout.

LAYOUT:
- Phone (360–390px): single column, 16px side margins, sticky top bar (logo "EduSaas" with a small "demo" tag, a language button "اردو", a theme toggle), bottom tab bar with icons and labels (64px tall, active tab has a 3px navy bar).
- Desktop (960px+): the bottom bar becomes a 208px left side rail; content max 1040px wide.
- Touch targets at least 44px. Buttons 48px tall, 10px corners. One primary action per screen.

COMPONENTS to reuse everywhere: cards; status badges (pill: green "Cleared", red "Pending", amber "Waiting", grey "Coming soon"/"Draft"); topic chips (a 44px rounded square with the topic number, e.g. "1.2", accent colours); stat tiles (big number + small label); progress ring and thin progress bars (accent); bottom sheet dialogs (phone) and centred dialogs (desktop); segmented controls; tabs as pill buttons; toast messages; skeleton loaders; an offline banner (amber); empty states with one helpful sentence; line icons (2px stroke, rounded).

SUBJECT ICONS: Physics = atom, Chemistry = flask, Biology = leaf, Mathematics = sigma, English = lines of text, Computer Science = </> code.

ACCESSIBILITY: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, never colour alone (always icon + text for status), visible focus rings in teal.

Use realistic demo data: college "Margalla Heights College (Demo)"; class "11th Pre-Medical A"; student Ali Raza (roll 11A-01); parent Mrs. Fatima Raza; teacher Mr. Tariq Mehmood (Physics); admin Ms. Sana Javed. Physics Unit 1 "Physical Quantities and Measurements" has three topics: 1.1 Estimation of Physical Quantities (3:30, pages 8–10), 1.2 Derived Units in Terms of Base Units (2:13, pages 10–11), 1.3 Dimensions of Physical Quantities (3:40, pages 11–14).

Start with the Sign in screen.
```

---

## 2. Screen prompts

### Everyone

**2.1 Sign in**

```text
Sign in screen, phone. Centred navy app mark (book with play triangle), title "Sign in", subtitle "For students, teachers and parents registered by your college."
Card: label "Mobile number", input with a fixed "+92" prefix box and placeholder "3001234567", primary button "Send code".
Below: an info banner with a shield icon: "Only numbers registered by the college can sign in. Each account sees only its own class, child or record."
A collapsed "Demo accounts (for presenters)" row at the bottom.
Also design the second step on the same screen: "We sent a 6-digit code to +92 399 2220001. Change", a large centred 6-digit code input with wide letter spacing, "Resend code in 30s", and an error state "That code is wrong. 4 tries left." in red.
Show a small toast-like card at the top: "SMS · EduSaas — Your sign-in code is 482913. It expires in 5 minutes."
```

**2.2 Shared states**

```text
Design a sheet of shared states for EduSaas, phone width: (1) skeleton loading cards, (2) offline banner "You are offline. Reconnect to continue; your progress so far is saved." with a wifi-off icon, (3) error card "Could not load this page" with "Try again", (4) empty state "No messages yet.", (5) toast "Attendance saved.", (6) a bottom-sheet dialog with title, body text, error line and Cancel / primary buttons.
```

### Student

**2.3 Student home**

```text
Student home, phone. Top: date "Thursday, October 1", greeting "Assalam o alaikum, Ali", "11th Pre-Medical A · Roll 11A-01", and on the right a progress ring "33%" with caption "1/3 topics".
An amber "Pending clearance" card with a warning icon: "You were absent on Thu, Oct 1 and missed Physics 1.2 Derived Units in Terms of Base Units. Listen to the lesson and score 4/5 in the quiz to be cleared for class." Attempts line "Attempts: 1 · best 3/5". Full-width navy button with play icon "Start missed lesson".
A green "Cleared for class" card: "1.1 Estimation of Physical Quantities · passed with 4/5".
Section "MY SUBJECTS": a card per live subject (Physics: atom icon tile, "1 of 3 topics done", red badge "1 missed", thin teal progress bar). Then a collapsed row "Coming soon · Chemistry, Biology".
Bottom tabs: Home (active), Library, Log out.
```

**2.4 Subject page**

```text
Subject page for Physics, phone. Back link "Home". Large atom icon tile, title "Physics", "Grade 11 · 1 of 14 units available".
Section "UNIT 1 · PHYSICAL QUANTITIES AND MEASUREMENTS" with three topic cards: chip "1.1", title, meta row with clock "3:30" and page icon "Pages 8–10", and a status badge on the right (green "✓ 4/5", amber "Quiz ready", grey "45% heard", red "Missed").
Section "MORE UNITS · COMING SOON": compact greyed rows with the unit number chip, title (Vectors, Translatory Motion, Rotational and Circular Motion, …) and a grey "Coming soon" badge.
Also show the version for a subject with no content: a dashed card with a clock icon "Chemistry is coming soon — Lessons appear here after the EduSaas team produces them and your teacher approves them."
```

**2.5 Library**

```text
Course library, phone. Title "Course library", "11th Pre-Medical A · 3 subjects". A horizontally scrolling row of pill tabs with subject icons: Physics (selected, navy), Chemistry "soon", Biology "soon". Under it, the selected subject's units (as on the subject page). At the bottom: "GRADE 12 · COMING SOON" with greyed pills Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics, English, Computer Science, and a small centred note "Units are added as the Content Factory produces them and teachers approve them."
```

**2.6 Lesson player** (the most important screen)

```text
Lesson player, phone. Breadcrumb "Home / Physics / Unit 1". Chip "1.2" + title "Derived Units in Terms of Base Units", meta "2:13 · Textbook pages 10, 11", badges red "Missed lecture" and grey "Draft, not yet reviewed".
Page tabs "p. 10" (selected) "p. 11" and a checkbox "Follow audio" on the right.
A large scanned textbook page placeholder (portrait, A4 ratio, white, looks like a photographed book page with headings and equations) with a dark pill "Tap to zoom" in the corner.
Small grey credit line "Physics Grade 11, National Book Foundation."
A caption card with a teal left border: label "NOW EXPLAINING", text "Pehla example: Force. Force barabar mass into acceleration…" (Roman Urdu).
A segmented control "Narration: English mix | اردو".
Docked at the bottom above the tab bar: a player with a segmented progress bar (10 segments, heard ones teal, current one navy), "45% heard · section 4 of 10" and "1:02 / 2:13", controls "-10s", previous, a 56px round navy play button, next, "+10s", speed "1x". Below the controls a full-width button: locked state "🔒 Quiz unlocks at 90% heard" (disabled, grey) and unlocked state "✓ Start quiz" (teal).
A collapsible "Full transcript (Roman Urdu)" list where the current section is highlighted in the accent tint.
```

**2.7 Quiz**

```text
Quiz question, phone. Back link "Back to lesson". Header "Physics · 1.2 quiz" and "Question 2 of 5", a thin progress bar. Card with the question "The joule (J) in terms of SI base units is:" and four full-width answer buttons with letter badges A–D ("kg m s⁻²", "kg m² s⁻³", "kg m² s⁻²", "kg m⁻² s²"); the selected one has a navy outline and a filled navy letter badge. Bottom: "Back" and primary "Next" (last question: "Submit answers"). Small centred note "You need 4 of 5 correct to pass."
```

**2.8 Quiz result**

```text
Two result screens, phone.
PASS: big green circle with a check, score "5/5", "Great job, you passed!", green badge "Cleared for class", "Your parent and your teacher have been told.", button "Back to home", light confetti.
FAIL: amber circle with a refresh icon, score "3/5", "Almost there!", "You need 4/5 to pass. Review the lesson, then try again in 30 seconds.", buttons "Review lesson" and primary "Try again".
Both followed by "REVIEW YOUR ANSWERS": a card per question with a green or amber left border, the question, "You chose: …" and "Correct: …" in bold, and a one-line grey explanation.
```

### Teacher

**2.9 My classes**

```text
Teacher "My classes", phone. Date, name "Mr. Tariq Mehmood", college name. Section header "MY CLASSES" with a small outlined button "+ Add subject" on the right. Cards per class+subject with the subject icon tile: "11th Pre-Medical A · Physics · 6 students"; another "11th Pre-Medical A · Mathematics · 6 students" with a grey "Coming soon" badge.
Section "YOUR SUBJECT REQUESTS": a greyed card "English · Waiting for college admin" (amber badge) and one "Declined" (red badge) with the admin's note and a "Dismiss" link.
An "Alerts on this phone" card: "Get a notification when a student you teach is cleared." with a "Turn on" button.
Bottom tabs: My classes (active), Alerts log, Log out.
```

**2.10 Class: attendance and clearance**

```text
Teacher class page, phone. Back "My classes", "Thursday, October 1 · Physics", title "11th Pre-Medical A". Three stat tiles: Present 5 (green), Absent 1, Pending 1 (amber).
A card with a WhatsApp-green border "Tell parents on WhatsApp" and badge "1 not told yet": "Free: each button opens your WhatsApp with the message ready. Tap Send there." Row: avatar "AR", "Mrs. Fatima Raza, parent of Ali Raza", green WhatsApp button "Send on WhatsApp".
Section "CLASS CLEARANCE": rows with avatar initials, name, "1.2 Derived Units · absent Thu, Oct 1", "Last attempt today 4:10 pm · best 3/5 · 2 attempts", red "Pending" badge and a text button "Clear manually…"; another row with green "✓ Cleared" "Passed 5/5, today 11:42".
Section "TODAY'S ATTENDANCE" with a green "Submitted" badge: dropdown "Topic taught today: 1.2 Derived Units in Terms of Base Units", help text "Absent students get this topic as their missed lecture, and their parents get an alert."
Roster card: each row avatar, name, "11A-02 · Mr. Imran Khan" with a small pencil icon, and two square toggle buttons "P" (filled green when present) and "A" (filled red when absent; the absent student's avatar turns red).
Sticky bar above the bottom tabs: "All present" and primary "Save changes · 1 absent" (when nothing changed: a disabled green "✓ Saved").
```

**2.11 Teacher dialogs**

```text
Three bottom sheets, phone:
(1) "Clear Ali Raza manually": text "1.2 Derived Units in Terms of Base Units. The reason is saved with the record, and the parent gets an alert." Radio list: Medical certificate provided (selected), On official college duty, Covered the topic with the teacher in person, Other (reveals a text area). Buttons Cancel / "Clear for class".
(2) "Parent's mobile number": "Mrs. Fatima Raza, parent of Ali Raza. Absence alerts go to this number." +92 phone input, inline error "Enter a 10-digit mobile number starting with 3.", Cancel / "Save number".
(3) "Add a subject": class dropdown, radio list of subjects with icons; Physics and Mathematics disabled with a green "You teach this" badge, Chemistry disabled "Already taught here", English and Computer Science selectable with a grey "Coming soon" badge. Cancel / "Send request".
```

**2.12 Alerts log**

```text
Teacher "Alerts log", phone. Intro "Every alert about students in your classes: in-app alerts, phone notifications, and the WhatsApp messages you sent." A chat-style panel with a dark green header "Margalla Heights College (Demo) · Alerts sent to parents and teachers". Message bubbles (light green) each with a small teal "To parent: Mrs. Fatima Raza · +92 399 3330001" line, the message text, and a footer "In app · sent to 1 phone · today 10:40" or "WhatsApp, sent by the teacher · today 10:41 ✓✓".
```

### Parent

**2.13 Parent home**

```text
Parent home, phone, for Mrs. Fatima Raza. Child card for "Ali Raza, 11th Pre-Medical A · Roll 11A-01" with an amber badge "1 to clear" (or green "Up to date").
Three stat tiles: "80%" Attendance (8 of 10 classes, 30 days), "1/3" Topics done, "4.3/5" Average quiz score.
Lines with icons: "⚠ Absent Thu, Oct 1: must complete Physics 1.3 Dimensions of Physical Quantities (not started yet)" and "✓ Cleared Physics 1.1 Estimation, Sep 29".
"Subjects": rows with subject icon, "Physics · 1 of 3 topics · avg 4/5", progress bar and a chevron; greyed rows "Chemistry · Coming soon".
"Recent attendance": a strip of 7 small day tiles (Mon P green … Thu A red).
"Last studied today at 4:10 pm · usually clears missed lectures in 1 day".
Below: "Alerts on this phone" card with "Turn on", "MESSAGES FROM THE COLLEGE" (last 4 messages, chat style) with "See all 6 messages", and a "Weekly summary — Every Sunday evening, a short progress report in Messages" row with a toggle switch.
Bottom tabs: My child, Messages, Log out. Read-only: no edit buttons anywhere.
```

**2.14 Child's subject detail**

```text
Parent view of one subject, phone. Back link "Ali Raza". Atom icon tile, title "Physics", "Ali Raza · 11th Pre-Medical A". Info banner: "After each lesson there is a 5-question quiz. 4 correct answers is a pass. A missed lecture is cleared when the quiz is passed."
"UNIT 1 · …" card with a row per topic: chip "1.1", title, an optional coloured sub-line ("Missed, now cleared" green / "Missed lecture, not cleared yet" amber), and a status badge on the right: green "✓ Passed 4/5", grey "Listening (45% heard)", amber "Quiz ready", grey "— Not started". Footer "13 more units coming soon."
```

**2.15 Messages**

```text
Parent "Messages", phone. Chat-style list from "Margalla Heights College (Demo)". Show three kinds: absence alert ("Dear Parent, Ali Raza was marked absent today in Physics…", footer "In app · sent to 1 phone"), the same message "WhatsApp, sent by the teacher ✓✓", and a weekly summary ("Weekly summary, Mon 21 Sep to Sun 27 Sep. Ali Raza: present in 6 of 6 classes. Physics 1 of 3 topics, average quiz 4/5. Chemistry, Biology: coming soon.", footer "In app"). Footnote explaining that alerts are free.
```

### College admin

**2.16 Admin home**

```text
College admin home, phone. Title "Margalla Heights College (Demo)", "College admin · Ms. Sana Javed". Four tappable stat tiles in a 2×2 grid: 8 Students, 3 Teachers, 8 Parents, 2 Classes.
"SUBJECT REQUESTS" with amber badge "1 waiting": card with Mathematics icon "Mathematics for 11th Pre-Medical A", "Asked by Mr. Tariq Mehmood · today 11:42 · no lessons yet (Coming soon)", buttons "Decline…" and primary "Approve".
"RECENT ACTIVITY" with a "See all" link: rows like "Imported students: 2 students, 1 parent — Ms. Sana Javed · today 11:51", "Imran Ali: suspended: Moved to another college".
Bottom tabs: Home, People, Classes, Import, Log out.
```

**2.17 People**

```text
Admin "People", phone. Title with a navy "+ Add" button. Pill tabs Students (selected) / Teachers / Parents. Search field "Search by name, phone or roll number". A list card: avatar, bold name, grey line "+92 399 2220001 · 11th Pre-Medical A · Roll 11A-01 · parent Mrs. Fatima Raza", chevron. One row dimmed with a red "Suspended" badge. Footer "8 shown".
Also design the "Add a student" bottom sheet: Full name, Mobile number (+92), Gender, Class dropdown, Roll number, a "PARENT" divider, Parent's mobile number, Parent's full name ("Leave blank if the parent is already registered"), note "They sign in with this number. Nobody else can use it.", buttons Cancel / "Add student".
And the edit sheet with an "ACCOUNT" section: reason field and a red-text "Suspend account" button (or "Reactivate account" when suspended).
```

**2.18 Classes**

```text
Admin "Classes", phone. Title with "+ New class". A card per class: section chip "A", "11th Pre-Medical A", "2026-2027 · Boys · 6 students"; "Teachers" list with subject icon, "Physics · Mr. Tariq Mehmood" and a small ✕ remove button per row; outlined button "+ Assign teacher".
Plus the "New class" sheet (Grade 11th/12th, Stream, Section, Students Boys/Girls/Mixed, Academic year) and the "Assign a teacher to 11th Pre-Medical A" sheet (Teacher dropdown, Subject dropdown with "(coming soon)" labels).
```

**2.19 Import**

```text
Admin "Import", phone. Intro "Add a whole class, or all your teachers, from a spreadsheet saved as CSV." Pill tabs "Students and parents" / "Teachers". Card with numbered steps: 1. "Download the template" link …, 2. choose the file or paste below, 3. "Check file — nothing is saved until you press Import". File picker, a monospace text area, primary "Check file".
Result state A (errors): amber card "1 row needs fixing — 2 rows checked · 1 OK · 1 with errors", section "FIX THESE ROWS, THEN CHECK AGAIN" with red row-number chips "3" and "Roll number 11A-01 already exists in 11th Pre-Medical A.", note "Row numbers match your spreadsheet (row 1 is the header)", and "ROWS THAT ARE OK" preview rows.
Result state B (clean): green card "Ready to import 2 rows", preview, primary "Import 2 rows"; then success "Imported — 2 students, 1 parent created. They can sign in with their numbers now."
```

**2.20 Activity log**

```text
Admin "Activity log", phone. Back "Home", intro "Every change in your college: who did it and when. Phone numbers are partly hidden." A card list of entries: summary text (e.g. "Added teacher Ms. Hira Saleem (+92 3** ***9005)") and grey "Ms. Sana Javed · today 11:50".
```

---

## 3. Variant prompts

**3.1 Desktop**

```text
Create desktop (1440×900) versions of: Student home, Lesson player, Teacher class page, Parent home, Admin People.
Replace the bottom tab bar with a 208px left side rail (icon + label, active item in accent tint with a 3px navy marker, "Log out" pinned at the bottom).
Lesson player: two columns: the textbook page on the left, sized to fit the window height; on the right the narration switch, caption, the player (not docked) and an open transcript.
Teacher class page: attendance roster on the left, clearance list on the right (sticky).
Student home: subject cards in a 3-column grid. Parent home: child cards two across. Admin People: a table with columns Name, Phone, Class/Roll, Parent, Status.
```

**3.2 Dark mode**

```text
Create dark-theme versions of Student home, Lesson player, Teacher class page and Parent home using: background #171A21, cards #21252E, borders #353B47, text #ECEEF3, secondary #A3ABBB, primary #7AA7E8 (with dark text #0E1522 on it), accent #3CC9B8, success #4ADE9B, warning #F5B94A, error #F58A80. Keep the textbook page area light (#D9D9D6) so the scan stays readable.
```

**3.3 Urdu (right to left)**

```text
Create Urdu versions of Sign in, Student home, Lesson player, Quiz and Parent home. Mirror the layout right to left (dir=rtl): the side rail on the right, back arrows pointing right, text right-aligned. Use Noto Nastaliq Urdu for Urdu text with line height 2; keep English names, class names, lesson titles, numbers, phone numbers and the audio controls left to right.
Labels: Home = ہوم, Library = لائبریری, My child = میرا بچہ, Messages = پیغامات, Log out = لاگ آؤٹ, Sign in = سائن ان, Send code = کوڈ بھیجیں, Pending clearance = کلیئرنس باقی ہے, Start missed lesson = رہ جانے والا سبق شروع کریں, My subjects = میرے مضامین, Coming soon = جلد آ رہا ہے, Start quiz = کوئز شروع کریں, Quiz unlocks at 90% heard = 90٪ سننے پر کوئز کھلے گا, Up to date = سب مکمل, Attendance = حاضری, Weekly summary = ہفتہ وار رپورٹ, Physics = فزکس, Chemistry = کیمسٹری, Biology = بیالوجی. Greeting: السلام علیکم، Ali.
The header language button shows "English" when Urdu is on.
```

**3.4 Tablet**

```text
Create tablet (768×1024 portrait and 1024×768 landscape) versions of the Lesson player and Teacher class page. Portrait: one column with wider cards and a two-column topic list. Landscape: two panes as on desktop, with the bottom tab bar replaced by the side rail.
```

---

## 4. Review checklist (before exporting)

- [ ] Every screen uses only the colours and type above; status is never shown by colour alone.
- [ ] Touch targets are at least 44px; the primary action is reachable with one thumb.
- [ ] The phone layout works at 360px wide with no sideways scrolling.
- [ ] Loading, empty, error and offline states exist for each list screen.
- [ ] Teacher attendance: one tap per student, Save always visible.
- [ ] Lesson player: page, caption, controls and the quiz button are all visible without scrolling on a 390×844 phone.
- [ ] Parent screens contain no edit actions.
- [ ] Urdu screens are mirrored, with numbers, names and media controls left to right.
- [ ] Dark mode keeps WCAG AA contrast.
- [ ] No real person's name, photo or phone number appears.

```text
- College admin: adds teachers, students and parents, imports a class from a spreadsheet, approves teachers' subject requests.

BRAND AND STYLE: calm, trustworthy, academic. Flat surfaces, 1px borders, soft 12px corners, no heavy shadows, no gradients, no stock photos, no emoji. Generous spacing. Feels like a well-made banking or government-services app, not a game.

COLOURS (light theme):
- Background #F5F6F9, cards #FFFFFF, sunken areas #EEF0F5, borders #DDE1EA
- Text #1B2130, secondary text #5A6478
- Primary (deep navy) #1E3A5F, text on primary #FFFFFF
- Accent (teal/emerald) #0F8F83, accent tint #E3F4F2
- Success #047857 on #E3F5EC; Pending/warning (amber) #A55A06 on #FFF3DC; Error/absent #B42318 on #FDECEA
- WhatsApp green for WhatsApp actions only: #128C7E
COLOURS (dark theme): background #171A21, cards #21252E, borders #353B47, text #ECEEF3, secondary #A3ABBB, primary #7AA7E8, accent #3CC9B8, success #4ADE9B, warning #F5B94A, error #F58A80.

TYPE: Inter (or Roboto). Body 16px minimum, line height 1.5. H1 22px bold on phones (26px desktop). Section labels 15px bold, uppercase, letter-spaced, secondary colour. Urdu text uses Noto Nastaliq Urdu with line height 2 and right-to-left layout.

LAYOUT:
- Phone (360–390px): single column, 16px side margins, sticky top bar (logo "EduSaas" with a small "demo" tag, a language button "اردو", a theme toggle), bottom tab bar with icons and labels (64px tall, active tab has a 3px navy bar).
- Desktop (960px+): the bottom bar becomes a 208px left side rail; content max 1040px wide.
- Touch targets at least 44px. Buttons 48px tall, 10px corners. One primary action per screen.

COMPONENTS to reuse everywhere: cards; status badges (pill: green "Cleared", red "Pending", amber "Waiting", grey "Coming soon"/"Draft"); topic chips (a 44px rounded square with the topic number, e.g. "1.2", accent colours); stat tiles (big number + small label); progress ring and thin progress bars (accent); bottom sheet dialogs (phone) and centred dialogs (desktop); segmented controls; tabs as pill buttons; toast messages; skeleton loaders; an offline banner (amber); empty states with one helpful sentence; line icons (2px stroke, rounded).

SUBJECT ICONS: Physics = atom, Chemistry = flask, Biology = leaf, Mathematics = sigma, English = lines of text, Computer Science = </> code.

ACCESSIBILITY: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, never colour alone (always icon + text for status), visible focus rings in teal.

Use realistic demo data: college "Margalla Heights College (Demo)"; class "11th Pre-Medical A"; student Ali Raza (roll 11A-01); parent Mrs. Fatima Raza; teacher Mr. Tariq Mehmood (Physics); admin Ms. Sana Javed. Physics Unit 1 "Physical Quantities and Measurements" has three topics: 1.1 Estimation of Physical Quantities (3:30, pages 8–10), 1.2 Derived Units in Terms of Base Units (2:13, pages 10–11), 1.3 Dimensions of Physical Quantities (3:40, pages 11–14).

Start with the Sign in screen.
```

# Stitch prompts for the EduSaas UI

As of 1 October 2026 · For: Google Stitch (AI UI design) · Feeds: F1, the React rebuild

This pack describes every screen of the EduSaas app so Stitch can design them in one consistent style. The designs then guide F1. The design tokens below are the ones the app uses today, so the designs and the code stay in step.

## How to use it

1. Create one Stitch project called **EduSaas**. Choose **Mobile** first.
2. Paste the **master prompt** (section 1) as the first message. It sets the product, users, brand and components for every later screen.
3. Paste the screen prompts (section 2) one at a time, in the same project, so Stitch reuses the style. Each prompt stands on its own if you need to regenerate one.
4. After the mobile screens, run the **variant prompts** (section 3) for desktop, dark mode and Urdu.
5. Check every screen against the **review checklist** (section 4) before exporting to Figma or code.

Notes:
- **Textbook pages:** Stitch can't show the real National Book Foundation pages. Prompts ask for a "scanned textbook page placeholder", and the real page goes in during build.
- **People:** every name and phone number is fictional (the demo uses the unissued `+92 399` range).
- **Iterating:** keep prompts short when you revise one screen, for example "Make the Submit button sticky above the bottom bar."

---

## 1. Master prompt (paste first)

```text
Design a mobile-first web app (installable PWA) called EduSaas, for FBISE intermediate colleges in Pakistan.

WHAT IT DOES: When a student misses a class, they get the exact textbook lesson they missed as a narrated page: the scanned textbook page on screen, with audio narration that follows the page. After listening to 90% they take a 5-question quiz; 4 correct = "Cleared for class". The parent gets an alert, and the teacher sees a green "Cleared" tick. The college admin registers everyone. The only way in is a phone number registered by the college.

USERS (4 roles, each with their own home screen):
- Student (16–18, low-end Android phone, patchy mobile data): catches up on missed lessons, studies by subject.
- Teacher: takes attendance in under a minute, sees who is cleared, tells parents on WhatsApp with one tap.
- Parent (often reads Urdu more easily than English, may not be tech-savvy): sees their child's attendance, progress and alerts. Read-only.
- College admin: adds teachers, students and parents, imports a class from a spreadsheet, approves teachers' subject requests.

BRAND AND STYLE: calm, trustworthy, academic. Flat surfaces, 1px borders, soft 12px corners, no heavy shadows, no gradients, no stock photos, no emoji. Generous spacing. Feels like a well-made banking or government-services app, not a game.

COLOURS (light theme):
- Background #F5F6F9, cards #FFFFFF, sunken areas #EEF0F5, borders #DDE1EA
- Text #1B2130, secondary text #5A6478
- Primary (deep navy) #1E3A5F, text on primary #FFFFFF
- Accent (teal/emerald) #0F8F83, accent tint #E3F4F2
- Success #047857 on #E3F5EC; Pending/warning (amber) #A55A06 on #FFF3DC; Error/absent #B42318 on #FDECEA
- WhatsApp green for WhatsApp actions only: #128C7E
COLOURS (dark theme): background #171A21, cards #21252E, borders #353B47, text #ECEEF3, secondary #A3ABBB, primary #7AA7E8, accent #3CC9B8, success #4ADE9B, warning #F5B94A, error #F58A80.

TYPE: Inter (or Roboto). Body 16px minimum, line height 1.5. H1 22px bold on phones (26px desktop). Section labels 15px bold, uppercase, letter-spaced, secondary colour. Urdu text uses Noto Nastaliq Urdu with line height 2 and right-to-left layout.

LAYOUT:
- Phone (360–390px): single column, 16px side margins, sticky top bar (logo "EduSaas" with a small "demo" tag, a language button "اردو", a theme toggle), bottom tab bar with icons and labels (64px tall, active tab has a 3px navy bar).
- Desktop (960px+): the bottom bar becomes a 208px left side rail; content max 1040px wide.
- Touch targets at least 44px. Buttons 48px tall, 10px corners. One primary action per screen.

COMPONENTS to reuse everywhere: cards; status badges (pill: green "Cleared", red "Pending", amber "Waiting", grey "Coming soon"/"Draft"); topic chips (a 44px rounded square with the topic number, e.g. "1.2", accent colours); stat tiles (big number + small label); progress ring and thin progress bars (accent); bottom sheet dialogs (phone) and centred dialogs (desktop); segmented controls; tabs as pill buttons; toast messages; skeleton loaders; an offline banner (amber); empty states with one helpful sentence; line icons (2px stroke, rounded).

SUBJECT ICONS: Physics = atom, Chemistry = flask, Biology = leaf, Mathematics = sigma, English = lines of text, Computer Science = </> code.

ACCESSIBILITY: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, never colour alone (always icon + text for status), visible focus rings in teal.

Use realistic demo data: college "Margalla Heights College (Demo)"; class "11th Pre-Medical A"; student Ali Raza (roll 11A-01); parent Mrs. Fatima Raza; teacher Mr. Tariq Mehmood (Physics); admin Ms. Sana Javed. Physics Unit 1 "Physical Quantities and Measurements" has three topics: 1.1 Estimation of Physical Quantities (3:30, pages 8–10), 1.2 Derived Units in Terms of Base Units (2:13, pages 10–11), 1.3 Dimensions of Physical Quantities (3:40, pages 11–14).

```

Use Noto Nastaliq Urdu for Urdu text with line height 2; keep English names, class names, lesson titles, numbers, phone numbers and the audio controls left to right.
```text
Labels: Home = ہوم, Library = لائبریری, My child = میرا بچہ, Messages = پیغامات, Log out = لاگ آؤٹ, Sign in = سائن ان, Send code = کوڈ بھیجیں, Pending clearance = کلیئرنس باقی ہے, Start missed lesson = رہ جانے والا سبق شروع کریں, My subjects = میرے مضامین, Coming soon = جلد آ رہا ہے, Start quiz = کوئز شروع کریں, Quiz unlocks at 90% heard = 90٪ سننے پر کوئز کھلے گا, Up to date = سب مکمل, Attendance = حاضری, Weekly summary = ہفتہ وار رپورٹ, Physics = فزکس, Chemistry = کیمسٹری, Biology = بیالوجی. Greeting: السلام علیکم، Ali.
The header language button shows "English" when Urdu is on.
```

**3.4 Tablet**

```text
Create tablet (768×1024 portrait and 1024×768 landscape) versions of the Lesson player and Teacher class page. Portrait: one column with wider cards and a two-column topic list. Landscape: two panes as on desktop, with the bottom tab bar replaced by the side rail.
```

---

## 4. Review checklist (before exporting)

- [ ] Every screen uses only the colours and type above; status is never shown by colour alone.
- [ ] Touch targets are at least 44px; the primary action is reachable with one thumb.
- [ ] The phone layout works at 360px wide with no sideways scrolling.
- [ ] Loading, empty, error and offline states exist for each list screen.
- [ ] Teacher attendance: one tap per student, Save always visible.
- [ ] Lesson player: page, caption, controls and the quiz button are all visible without scrolling on a 390×844 phone.
- [ ] Parent screens contain no edit actions.
- [ ] Urdu screens are mirrored, with numbers, names and media controls left to right.
- [ ] Dark mode keeps WCAG AA contrast.
- [ ] No real person's name, photo or phone number appears.

# F1: Design system and responsive shell (React + TypeScript + Vite PWA)

Status: Signed off 2026-10-01 (instructions "continue with the whole development" and "continue with F1") · Owner: Muhammad Noor Khan · Last updated: 2026-10-01

Roadmap: [Responsive UI rebuild](../roadmap.md#responsive-ui-rebuild) · Decision D1 (React + TypeScript + Vite PWA), D2 (no separate app) · Designs: [Stitch prompt pack](../stitch-ui-prompts.md)

## Problem

The web app is about 1,900 lines of hand-written JavaScript in one file, building HTML from strings. It works and is tested in the browser, but it has no components, no types and no unit tests, so every change risks breaking another screen. A team can't safely share it. It also can't take the Stitch designs without rewriting screens by hand. F1 rebuilds it on React, TypeScript and Vite, as a set of reusable components on design tokens, next to the current app, so the demo never breaks.

## Users and access rules

No change. Every rule is enforced by the Django API, which the new app calls unchanged. The new app only decides what to show for the signed-in role, as the current app does.

## Screens

- **Built next to the current app:** the new app is served at `/app/`, while the current app stays at `/`. Screens move over in the roadmap's order:
  1. **Foundation:** tokens, components, the gallery page `/app/#/gallery`, and the app shell (header, bottom tab bar on phones, side rail at 960 px and up, theme, language and right-to-left).
  2. **Sign-in, student home, subject, library.**
  3. **Lesson player, quiz and result.**
  4. **Parent:** home, child detail, messages.
  5. **Teacher:** classes, attendance and clearance, dialogs, alerts log.
  6. **College admin:** home, people, classes, import, activity.
  7. **Switch-over:** `/` serves the new app once its browser tests pass, and the old app is removed.
- **Look:** the same as today (same tokens), so the switch is invisible to users. The Stitch designs are applied afterwards through the tokens and components.

## API and data changes

None to the API. Frontend structure:
- `web/`: a Vite project (React 18, TypeScript in strict mode).
- `web/src/tokens.css`: the design tokens.
- `web/src/ui/`: components.
- `web/src/screens/`: one folder per role.
- `web/src/api.ts`: a typed API client.
- `web/src/i18n/`: English keys and Urdu, moved from `demo/i18n.js`.
- **Build:** `npm run build` outputs to `web/dist`. Django serves it at `/app/`. In development, Vite proxies `/api` and `/media` to Django.
- **Service worker and manifest:** reused from F3 (push).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given `npm run build`, then the first load is at most 150 KB of compressed JavaScript.
2. Given the gallery page, then every component renders at 360, 768 and 1440 px, in light, dark and right-to-left.
3. Given each migrated screen, then a browser test signs in as the right role and completes the same journey as on the old app (for example, mark absent, listen, pass the quiz, cleared).

content.text:
The Stitch prompt is ready, and every screen of the app has been rebuilt for F1 in React and TypeScript. The new app looks and behaves the same as the current one, and passed a full browser test of every role's journey. The current app stays the default until you approve the switch.

**Stitch prompt**

It's at [docs/stitch-ui-prompts.md](docs/stitch-ui-prompts.md). Paste the **master prompt** into Stitch first: it sets the product, the four user roles, your exact colours and fonts, the layout rules, the components and the demo data. Then paste the **20 screen prompts** one at a time in the same Stitch project:
- sign-in and shared states
- student: home, subject, library, lesson player, quiz, result
- teacher: classes, attendance and clearance, dialogs, alerts log
- parent: home, child's subject, messages
- admin: home, people, classes, import, activity

After those come **variant prompts** for desktop, dark mode, Urdu right-to-left and tablet, and a **review checklist** to go through before exporting.

**F1 progress**
- **Where:** the new app lives in `web/` and is served at **http://localhost:8000/app/**. The current app stays at `/`.
- **What's done:** all 18 screens for the four roles, built on shared components, with a component gallery at `/app/#/gallery`. It keeps the same look, Urdu support and free phone alerts.
- **Easy to restyle:** all styling comes from shared colour settings and components, so applying your Stitch designs later means changing those rather than every screen.
- **Size:** 77 KB of JavaScript per page load, about half the 150 KB budget.
- **Starting it:** `start-demo.bat` now also builds the new app when Node.js is installed, and skips it with a message if not. The current app at `/` works without Node.

**Tests:** all pass.

| What | Result |
|---|---|
| Type-checking | No errors |
| New-app unit tests | 12 pass |
| Browser test of the new app | 25 checks pass, no page errors |
| Backend tests | 76 pass |

The browser test covered:
- a stranger being refused
- a teacher marking an absence and sending the WhatsApp message
- a student playing the lesson, switching to Urdu narration, passing the quiz and getting cleared
- the teacher seeing the green tick, and the parent seeing their child's progress
- an admin adding a teacher and importing a roster (a bad row refused, then a clean file saved)
- the Urdu interface
- the gallery at three widths in light, dark and Urdu, with no sideways scrolling

**Still open in F1**
1. **Switching `/` to the new app and removing the old one.** I've held this for your approval because it changes what everyone sees.
2. **Browser tests not yet written:** the page zoom, and the teacher's "Clear manually" and "parent number" dialogs.
3. **Not yet run:** accessibility and speed checks, and tablet-size screenshots.

When your Stitch designs are ready, share them and I'll apply them. Say "switch over" whenever you want the new app at `/`; I'd do item 2 first so those screens are tested before the old app goes.

"""Stage 1: render textbook pages to WebP (max 1080 px wide, per the architecture brief)."""
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

from .util import log

MAX_WIDTH = 1080
DEFAULT_WIDTH = 900  # the scanned pages are ~826 px wide, so 900 keeps full detail


def render_pages(pdf_path, page_numbers, out_dir, offset=0, width=DEFAULT_WIDTH, force=False):
    """Render book pages to <out_dir>/p<N>.webp. Returns {page_number: path}. Skips existing files."""
    import pymupdf

    width = min(width, MAX_WIDTH)
    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    result, doc = {}, None
    for n in sorted(set(page_numbers)):
        target = out_dir / f"p{n}.webp"
        result[n] = target
        if target.exists() and not force:
            continue
        if doc is None:
            doc = pymupdf.open(pdf_path)
        index = n - 1 + offset
        if not 0 <= index < doc.page_count:
            raise ValueError(f"page {n} is outside the PDF ({doc.page_count} pages, offset {offset})")
        page = doc[index]
        zoom = width / page.rect.width
        pix = page.get_pixmap(matrix=pymupdf.Matrix(zoom, zoom))
        img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (pix.width, pix.height), pix.samples)
        img.save(target, "WEBP", quality=70)
        log.info("page %d -> %s (%d KB)", n, target.name, target.stat().st_size // 1024)
    return result

# EduSaas: instructions for Claude and other coding agents

EduSaas is an AI LMS for FBISE colleges in Pakistan. When a student is absent, they get the exact textbook lesson they missed as a narrated page ("Lesson Object") and must pass a quiz to be cleared. The parent gets a WhatsApp alert and the teacher sees a green tick. It is sold B2B to colleges.

## Documents

- **Every document you write goes in [docs/](docs/) as a Markdown (`.md`) file.** This covers plans, roadmaps, research, specs, reports, change registers and meeting notes. Do not create Claude Docs, hosted artifacts or Word files for project documents unless the user asks for that format.
- Name files in kebab-case (`docs/offline-sync-design.md`). Put feature specs in `docs/features/F<N>-<short-name>.md`, copied from [docs/features/_template.md](docs/features/_template.md).
- Add every new document to the table in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md).
- [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md) is the plan of record: the feature IDs (F1–F19), phases, gates and the quality process all come from it. Update it when a decision changes it.

## How features are built

Work one feature at a time, following the seven steps in [docs/roadmap.md](docs/roadmap.md#quality-process-for-each-feature):

1. Write the spec in `docs/features/` and get the user's sign-off before writing code.
2. Write acceptance criteria as tests, including at least one test that tries to break an access rule.
3. Build a thin end-to-end slice (model, API, screen, test).
4. Run all tests. A feature is not done until every item in its definition of done is ticked.

## Non-negotiable rules

- **Only registered, linked people can sign in.** A student belongs to a class, a teacher is assigned to classes, and a parent is linked to their own child. Refuse unregistered numbers with a clear message. Enforce role and relationship checks on the server for every endpoint. Never add an "any number works" or shared demo login.
- **Quiz answers never go to the client.** Scoring happens on the server.
- **Content is reviewed before students see it.** Lessons generated by the Content Factory stay `draft` until a subject teacher approves them.
- **Textbook pages are National Book Foundation material.** Keep them internal until permission is granted (change register CR-02).
- **Personal data:** never write phone numbers or OTPs to logs. Never send the user's email address to outside services.

## Project layout

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `content_factory/` | Offline pipeline: textbook PDF → page images, script and quiz (authored JSON or Claude), edge-tts narration → Lesson Objects in `output/` |
| `backend/` | Django 6 API (`lms` app): roster, OTP sign-in, attendance, clearance, quiz scoring, notifications, parent progress, college admin console (`admin_api.py`). Serves the web app. The Django admin panel is for superusers only. |
| `web/` | The web app (F1): React 18 + TypeScript + Vite, served by Django at `/` from `web/dist`. Components in `src/ui`, screens per role in `src/screens`, typed API client in `src/lib/api.ts`, Urdu in `src/i18n/ur.json`, gallery at `/#/gallery`. |
| `media/` | Lesson page images and audio, copied in by `import_lessons`, served at `/media/` |
| `legacy/` | The old vanilla JavaScript app, kept for reference only (not served). Delete when the team agrees. |
| `docs/` | All project documents |
| `start-demo.bat` / `start-demo.sh` | Install, migrate, seed the demo roster and run the server on port 8000 |

## Commands

```text
start-demo.bat                                        # run the demo (resets data; add --keep to keep it)
cd backend && python manage.py test lms               # backend tests (76)
cd content_factory && python -m pytest tests          # Content Factory tests (19)
cd web && npm run build                               # type-check and build the web app into web/dist (served at /)
cd web && npm test                                    # web app unit tests (12)
cd web && npm run dev                                 # dev server on :5173, proxies /api to Django on :8000
cd backend && python manage.py seed_demo              # reset the demo roster (runs seed_catalogue and import_lessons)
cd backend && python manage.py seed_catalogue         # create or update the subject catalogue (Grade 11 and 12)
cd backend && python manage.py send_weekly_summaries  # weekly parent summary (in-app); schedule for Sunday 18:00
cd backend && python manage.py create_college "<name>" --admin-phone 03xxxxxxxxx --admin-name "<name>"
cd backend && python manage.py import_lessons phy11   # load built lessons into the database
```

Demo accounts are listed in [README.md](README.md). The demo college and all `+92 399` numbers are fictional.

## Conventions

- Python: Django, plain function views wrapped by the `@api` decorator in `backend/lms/auth.py`. Every new endpoint declares its allowed roles and scopes its queries to the caller's relationships.
- Every change to access rules or the clearance workflow gets a test in `backend/lms/tests.py`.
- Frontend: mobile-first, design tokens in CSS variables, light and dark mode, touch targets of at least 44 px.
- Frontend code is TypeScript in strict mode; build every screen from the components in `web/src/ui` and the tokens in `web/src/styles.css`, so a redesign changes those, not each screen.
- Student and parent screens are bilingual (F23): wrap every visible English sentence in `t('…', {vars})` (or `tr` for rich text) from `useI18n()` and add the Urdu to `web/src/i18n/ur.json`. Keep book content (lesson titles, questions) as in the textbook. Check right-to-left layout at 360 px.
- Accessibility: no serious or critical axe issues; dim with colour (`--muted`), never with opacity, so text keeps 4.5:1 contrast; use `--accent-ink` for teal text.
- Use Claude model `claude-opus-5-5` for any content generation.
